verdict: Tesla's revenue jumped 26% to $28.2B on record deliveries, but operating profit fell 57% to just $398M — and a $1B paper gain on its SpaceX stake did much of the work in the bottom line.

kpis.label: Capex
kpis.note: +142% YoY — free cash flow went negative at -$1.1B

segments.name: Automotive
segments.note: Car sales, leasing and regulatory credits — up 23% YoY on record deliveries of 480,126, though regulatory credit revenue fell to $146M from $439M a year ago.

segments.name: Services and other
segments.note: Supercharging, service centers, parts and FSD (supervised-driving) subscriptions — active FSD subscriptions reached 1.48 million.

segments.name: Energy generation and storage
segments.note: Megapack battery systems and solar — storage deployments rose 41% to 13.5 GWh.

opex.name: Research & development
opex.note: AI, the Optimus robot and new vehicles — up 49% YoY, a big reason operating profit fell.

opex.name: Selling, general & administrative
opex.note: Selling cars and running the company day to day — up 45% YoY.

takeaways.title: Operating profit is thinning
takeaways.text: Operating income fell to $398M — a 1.4% margin — even as revenue hit a record. Price cuts and a 49% jump in R&D spending overwhelmed the delivery growth.

takeaways.title: Capex went vertical
takeaways.text: Spending on AI compute, factories and equipment hit $5.8B in one quarter, pushing free cash flow to -$1.1B — the growth bill is arriving before the growth pays.

takeaways.title: A paper gain did heavy lifting
takeaways.text: An unrealized $1,005M gain on Tesla's SpaceX stake sits inside other income. Without it, pre-tax profit would have been roughly $324M instead of $1,329M.

oneTimers: A $1,005M unrealized (paper) gain on Tesla's SpaceX equity stake is inside the $590M of 'other income, net' in the release — no cash changed hands. A $112M unrealized loss on digital assets partly offset it.

Stock-based compensation was $1,151M (vs $635M a year ago), swollen by the 2025 CEO Performance Award — a non-cash cost inside operating expenses. Non-GAAP net income was $1,153M ($0.33 a share) vs GAAP $1,114M ($0.32).
The tax line includes a one-off benefit from releasing valuation allowances on California deferred tax assets, which is why the effective tax rate was only about 15%.
otherDetail: Interest income of $422M and other income of $590M — mostly a $1,005M paper gain on Tesla's SpaceX stake, partly offset by a $112M paper loss on digital assets — less $81M of interest expense: a net +$931M.
follow100Note: The rows reconcile to $100 within a cent of rounding.
footerNote: Net income here is Tesla's total net income of $1,128M; $1,114M of it is attributable to common stockholders (the rest belongs to minority partners in subsidiaries).
